messages:
jamal: Heads up — small canary spike: fncall/strict_schema is rejecting ~3.7% of requests for r-frontend across eu-west1. noticed after the 09:12 deploy. sample payload attached.

olga: Ugh. Is that the new validator we enabled for tool outputs? :eyes:

jamal: yeah, strict=true on the canary slice. sample response that failed validation:
```json
{"tool": "calendar.create", "args": {"date": "2026-03-19", "title": "sync"}}
```
validator error: `expected object with keys [id, start_time, end_time], got missing id`.

mike: Do we have a fallback route configured for strict rejects? I thought rejects were supposed to fall back to permissive route.

kevin: Canary config says `on_reject: drop` for strict. That was intentional to catch dangerous shapes in canary.

sara: Drop semantics + bursty user traffic = visible errors. Console shows 502s but no breakdown on rejects vs other infra failures. we need better telemetry.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-19T09:11:43Z by @kevin to r-frontend/canary

jamal: We should do two things: 1) change canary policy to `on_reject: route_permissive` so we don't surface to users; 2) add a metric `fncall.rejects_by_validator` and a dashboard panel in /console for the canary slice.

olga: Agree 1). For 2) the current telemetry only emits `fncall.reject` with no validator tag. We need validator_name + score + route_id in the telemetry envelope.

mike: Also add a sampled payload logging flag so we can inspect failing outputs without logging everything. `fncall.validator.sample_rate=0.01` per-route.

kevin: I'm nervous about switching canary to permissive without addressing silent regressions. Maybe set `on_reject: route_permissive` but tag the request with `validation_flag=true` and increment a panic counter if rate > 2% for 10m. alert to #incidents.

jamal: Good compromise. For console UX: when you click a route in the dashboard we should show a tiny "validation" widget: reject rate, top failing validators, recent sampled payloads (linked but redact PII). Right now route_id in logs is sometimes missing which makes attribution hard.

olga: I can throw together a quick PR to add tags to telemetry (route_id, validator, score) and wire a panel. Will also add a toggle: `show-sampled-failures` so support can inspect.

mike: For rollout plan: rollback canary to previous deploy? or hotpatch validator to be more permissive?

kevin: Patch the canary config (policy) first — low risk. If reject rate drops we keep canary and monitor. If it stays high, rollback deploy.

sara: Also need a billing note: currently rejects count as tokens but may be billed differently if we route to permissive. ops/finance FYI.

jamal: Action items:
- @olga update telemetry PR with route_id + validator_name + score + sample flag (olga)
- @kevin patch canary policy to `route_permissive` + validation_tag + panic alert (kevin)
- @mike add console panel skeleton and a redact pipeline for sampled payloads (mike)
- @sara check billing/quotas impact and add a note to the change log (sara)

olga: will open PR in the next 30m. tagging here when ready. :thumbsup:

kevin: patch applied to canary in prod at 09:27. monitor for 15m.

deploy-bot: Canary policy updated by @kevin at 2026-03-19T09:27:12Z

mike: saw reject rate drop to 0.9% after the patch. console shows fewer 502s. need the telemetry tags to confirm validator-level trends.

jamal: Great. Leaving this thread open until we have the telemetry PR merged and the dashboard up. Thanks everyone.

olga: PR opened: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/489 — adds validator tags + sample flag.

sara: billing note posted in the change log under r-frontend canary entry.

jamal: closing loop — set alert threshold to 1.5% for canary; if exceeded for 5m auto-roll back. moving to monitoring backlog.
